first_impression.reaction: Didn't expect this from a wedding company. 'Flags the stories that do not hold up' and naming museum, encyclopaedia and church sources is exactly what gets me past the intro. Most of what Google gives me for this search is the evil spirits stuff copied from site to site. I skipped to the FAQ first like I always do, saw it says 'we could not find that origin documented' about rice, and went back to the top.

journey.quote: This guide sets out where each tradition really comes from, using museum, encyclopaedia and church sources, and flags the stories that do not hold up.
journey.reaction: Good. That's a claim I can check, and they actually follow through with links.

journey.quote: Our keep, adapt or skip calls are editorial judgement, not rules.
journey.reaction: Splitting fact from opinion is what I want. Most sites mix the two and call it advice.

journey.quote: Britannica records that a few sources suggest ancient cultures believed this, and that modern medicine has shown there is no such vein.
journey.reaction: Myth called out and sourced. I clicked through and it says what they say it does.

journey.quote: Smartraveller advises speaking to a lawyer to confirm validity.
journey.reaction: They point me at a government source and a lawyer instead of telling me they'll sort it all out. That's honest about the limits.

journey.quote: The white dress is a 186-year-old fashion that became tradition.
journey.reaction: 1840 to 2026, the maths checks out. Specific dates are what make me believe the rest.

journey.quote: Scholars disagree about that, and it is not well documented, so we would leave it out of your ceremony script.
journey.reaction: Which scholars? Everywhere else they link the source. Here, and in the opening definition of handfast, there's no link, so it's the one bit I'd have to check myself.

journey.quote: House rules like these are rarely published, so your Wedded Advisor confirms them with the venue in writing.
journey.reaction: Practical and it admits the info isn't public. 'In writing' is the right instinct. Still makes me wonder what the Advisor costs and whether the venue is paying them too.

journey.quote: Lebanese celebrations, at home or abroad, are known for the zaffe, a procession with drummers and dancers.
journey.reaction: No source here when nearly every other section has one. Minor, but it's noticeable.

journey.quote: Through Wonderland Concierge, one Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, start to finish.
journey.reaction: First time the page actually says what the service is. 'Payments' gets my attention: does that mean supplier money goes through you, and with a margin on top? Also, is 'Wonderland Concierge' a different product from Wedded Wonderland? The name changes and I can't tell.

journey.section: How to choose which traditions to keep
journey.quote: Here is how we would weigh the traditions in this guide for a destination wedding. It is our editorial view, not a rule.
journey.reaction: The table is useful. I'd screenshot it for my fiancée.

journey.quote: a Wedded Advisor will plan it with you from first idea to the last dance.
journey.reaction: After a whole article of evidence, the closing line goes soft. 'First idea to the last dance' is a brochure line. Tell me what's actually included.

unanswered_questions: How is the Wedded Advisor paid: a flat fee, a percentage, or commissions from venues and suppliers?
When the page says the Advisor handles 'payments', do supplier prices go through Wedded Wonderland with a mark-up?
Is 'Wonderland Concierge' the same thing as Wedded Wonderland, or a separate paid tier?
Is there a real wedding I can look at, with the actual budget, that used one of these blended ceremonies?
Who are the 'scholars' who disagree on handfasting as a trial marriage?

turn_offs_found.quote: a Wedded Advisor will plan it with you from first idea to the last dance.
turn_offs_found.why: Emotional sign-off instead of facts. The rest of the page earned my trust with sources, and this line spends some of it.

would_share_with: My fiancée, mainly for the keep/adapt/skip table
Probably a Reddit thread if someone repeats the vein-of-love thing

cta_reaction.quote: Through Wonderland Concierge, one Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, start to finish.
cta_reaction.why: The CTA comes after the evidence, not before, so it doesn't annoy me. I'd click to see the Concierge page, but I'm not enquiring until I know how the fee works and whether there's a cut from venues. That's for the service page, not this article.

top_3_changes: Use one name for the service. 'Wonderland Concierge' next to 'Wedded Wonderland' and 'Wedded Advisor' makes me wonder if it's a separate product. Also add a short plain line on what 'payments' means, or link to where that's explained.
Replace 'from first idea to the last dance' with something concrete about what the Advisor actually does, in keeping with the tone of the rest of the page.
Source the two unlinked claims (the handfasting 'scholars disagree' line and the zaffe description) so every factual section has a source like the rest.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic, finance background, wants proof)
No invented brand facts; fee model, commissions and real weddings listed as unanswered, not assumed
[[VERIFY]] markers and HTML comments treated as invisible
Fee model and prices treated as deferred, not must-fix, per orchestrator

open_questions.question: Is the 'Wonderland Concierge' link label meant to be 'Wedded Concierge' per brand terms? To a reader it looks like a separate product.
Fee model, supplier pricing and a real wedding with budget remain this persona's blockers to enquiring; confirm they stay deferred to service pages.

assumptions: Daniel arrived from a Google search for 'wedding traditions' with general curiosity, not while actively shortlisting planners, so relevance is moderate.
Linked sources were taken to say what the draft says; Daniel's spot-check is in character, not an actual verification.
